The value of engine maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) for the aviation industry was $27 billion in 2016 and is expected to reach $40 billion by 2026.
Turbofan engine failures contribute to 60% of all airplane failures.
The CMAPSS dataset contains data for 100 turbofan engines until failure, with the number of operational cycles to failure ranging from 128 to 362.
The BLSTM model with dropout regularization achieved an RMSE of 26.68, MAE of 20.56, and R^2 of 0.59 on the CMAPSS dataset.
The BLSTM model outperformed the standard LSTM model and a Linear Regression baseline in terms of RUL prediction accuracy.
The BLSTM model uses two LSTM layers, one processing the input sequence in the forward direction and the other in the backward direction.
The key pre-processing steps included removing low-variance and highly correlated features, adding an RUL feature, normalizing the data, and applying a power transformation.
The key hyperparameters tuned for the BLSTM model included learning rate, batch size, number of epochs, number of hidden layer units, dropout rate, and batch normalization.
The error metrics used to evaluate the RUL prediction models were MSE, RMSE, MAE, and R^2 score.
The paper mentions that there is still room for improvement in further reducing the error metrics and testing the model on other datasets.
Accurate RUL prediction is important for turbofan engines due to safety concerns, high costs associated with AOG events, and the need for effective MRO planning.
Model-based approaches for RUL prediction require a deep understanding of the turbomachinery and physics, while data-based approaches use the data history of the system.

Some of the data-based approaches mentioned in the literature review include Regression Analysis, Fuzzy Logic, Gradient Boosting, Neural Networks, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, and Relevance Vector Machines.
The CMAPSS dataset is a simulation framework developed by NASA for examining turbofan engine degradation and contains sensor measurements, operational settings, and cycles until failure.
The turbofan engine consists of key components like the Fan, Low Pressure Compressor, High Pressure Compressor, Combustor, High Pressure Turbine, and Low Pressure Turbine.
